thread:
alice: :rotating_light: paging SRE — we're seeing a spike in routing errors for inference requests from EU region, ~15% 5xxs and lots of retries. Not sure if it's model fallback or DNS.
ben: saw it too, started ~10m ago. Most requests are being routed to us-east despite eu cluster healthy.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0453 — Smart-routing anomalies, possible DNS/edge stale endpoints. Pager: oncall-nyc
oncall-nyc: I'm on it. Can folks post the symptom summary and any error traces you have?
alice: symptom: increased 502/504s, long tail latency for streamed responses, client retries. Toplog shows repeated fallback to variant "gpt-lite-v2" in us-east.
carol: that's odd — policies should prefer regional eu variants. I can query the routing decision logs.
ben: attaching quick curl to the edge health endpoint that clients hit:

```
curl -v https://inference-eu.redwood.example/api/v1/generate -H 'Host: inference.redwood.ai' 2>&1 | tail -n 40
```

ben: response shows `X-Edge-Host: us-east-edge-12` for a bunch of requests.
david: I pulled the smart-routing logs. Policy engine returned fallback -> us-east because of an apparent unreachable endpoint list for eu region: all eu endpoints marked unhealthy in cache.
alice: who touched routing policy in last hour? any deploys?
carol: I didn't push any policy changes. But there was an infra automation run that rolled out DNS updates for a subset of eu edges 12m ago.
eve: that matches our timeline. I see a DNS change with lower TTL that didn't propagate everywhere. Some edge caches have stale rrset pointing to old IPs that are now decommissioned.
oncall-nyc: So clients hit the edge, edge attempted to route to eu model cluster, got failures, policy dropped to fallback us-east variant — causing cross-region traffic + higher errors. Is that right?
alice: yes. Also noticed that some eu endpoints were flagged unhealthy due to TCP handshake timeouts when reaching stale IPs.
edge-team-bot: Automated note: purge-edge-cache job queued. Use `edgectl purge --zone eu --force` to expedite.
ben: trying a targeted purge for the impacted eu edge nodes now.

```
# purge run
edgectl purge --zone eu --nodes eu-edge-11,eu-edge-12 --force
```

ben: initiated at 1799991320
carol: I'm watching the routing cache metrics.
incident-bot: Page escalated to Platform leads (carol, david) at 1799991330
oncall-nyc: quick mitigation plan: 1) purge edge caches 2) force-refresh routing cache 3) temporarily raise success threshold so policy won't fallback to us-east for 5m 4) reach out to customers.
alice: agree. Also add short-term route hold to avoid oscillation.
david: I can bump the policy confidence threshold. Running command:

```
policyctl set --name smart-routing --param min_success_rate=0.60 --ttl-override=300
```

david: executed at 1799991365
carol: after purge, some eu endpoints are coming back healthy. Unhealthy count dropped from 9 -> 2.
ben: client-side errors dropped in last 30s. 5xx rate down to ~3%.
eve: DNS audit: the new eu A record change was partially rolled. Some authoritative servers still serving old rrset due to intermediate caching at provider X. TTLs were 300 but some caches honored higher values.
alice: that's the propagation delay. We need to update runbook: don't decommission IPs immediately after changing A records, wait at least 10x TTL in practice
oncall-nyc: Agree. For now, do we want to re-enable eu-preferred routing? I prefer to hold until caches stable.
david: hold in place for 10m and monitor. Also I will spin a temporary redirect rule to drop cross-region retries for warm clients.
carol: posting diagnostic snippet for the routing cache showing timestamps:

```
2026-03-15T14:45:12Z route eu-cluster-1 -> 10.2.5.12 status=stale cached_at=1799990800 ttl=300
2026-03-15T14:46:05Z route eu-cluster-2 -> 10.2.5.13 status=healthy cached_at=1799991350 ttl=300
```

carol: that stale cached_at is from earlier change — explains mismatch.
ben: I'm going to rollback the decommission on the old IPs for another 15m so the OS-level retries succeed.
alice: please coordinate with infra so we don't create split-brain.
eve: notifying registrar/provider support to ask for cache flush or lower caching for the affected zones — opened ticket #REG-4432.
oncall-nyc: Customer impact: customer-ops, what's the customer-visible symptom and impacted customers?
customer-ops: multiple enterprise customers in EU reported degraded inference latency and occasional 502s in the last 20m. No data loss. Some heavy-traffic customers auto-retried and absorbed errors, but a couple hit rate limits and saw partial failures.
alice: prepping status update — short note: partial routing failure causing elevated errors for EU customers, mitigation in progress.
customer-ops: we'll send a brief to impacted accounts in 10m. Please call out no PII and actions taken.
ben: after purge+policy bump, error rate stabilized. We'll keep monitoring and plan to fully revert the policy once TTL propagation confirmed.
david: scheduling a follow-up postmortem: root cause likely DNS/edge cache mismatch leading to unhealthy marking and fallback policy triggering cross-region failover. Action items: update decommission procedure, add preflight checks before decommission, improve telemetry to detect partial DNS propagation earlier.
carol: logging an immediate action: add healthcheck that verifies routing cache consistency across regions and flags partial stale rrset.
eve: provider responded: they will attempt an expedited cache refresh. No guarantee.
oncall-nyc: Good work. Keep this thread updated every 5m until we mark INC-2026-0453 resolved.
incident-bot: Incident status: Mitigating -> Monitoring. Assigned: carol, david, ben. Severity downgraded to Sev2 at 1799991560
alice: I'll drop a short chronology for postmortem later.
customer-ops: we sent an update at 1799991600 to impacted customers; they acknowledged.
ben: last check: 5xxs ~0.7% now, regional routing back to eu cluster for most traffic.
carol: leaving a note to revert policy change at 1799991890 if metrics stable.

```
# automatic revert scheduled
at 1799991890: policyctl set --name smart-routing --param min_success_rate=0.35
```

carol: revert executed at 1799991895. Monitoring continues.
oncall-nyc: marking this thread for postmortem. Will handoff to day shift for follow-up.
alice: thanks everyone, nice fast coordination. We'll run the full postmortem and link here.
